Answers whether the geometry predicts taxonomic relations it never trained on, or only memorises the training closure -- Burkhard's objection to Figure 4.
why: Two prior gates in this project failed for two DIFFERENT wrong reasons on the SAME mistake: Task 9's frozen gate (b) could not distinguish a CONVERGED arm from a NEVER-TRAINED one (flat final-phase loss means both); amendment 2 fixed that and was then blind to Task 8's fixed arm, whose loss ROSE 3.90->4.02 while its S_angle simultaneously ROSE 0.892->0.933 -- the model improved throughout even though the proxy said otherwise. The common cause is that training loss is a proxy for the quantity of interest, and here the two arms' losses are not even the same quantity (vis00 vs vis50 take different numbers of optimizer steps per epoch; RandomDAG trains against a different closure entirely). P2 therefore has NO training-loss gate at all -- see validity_gate below for the replacement design and the reasoning stated in the artifact itself, not just in this session's prose.

Built from src/taxembed/eval/randomdag.py::randomize_parents(parent, depth, seed): every non-root node keeps its own DEPTH exactly but is rewired to a uniformly random parent at depth-1, so the closure's pair count (= sum of depth over all nodes) is preserved exactly, not approximately. The arm holds out parent edges from the RANDOMISED tree and is scored against the RANDOMISED parents -- its own held-out node set and candidate pools are built from the randomised closure, not the real one. It asks whether the model does as well on a scrambled taxonomy as on the real one: if it does, the geometry is memorising tree SHAPE (depth, branching pattern), not taxonomy. Because pool sizes (grandparent fan-out) are not preserved by the rewiring, this arm's own baselines.sibling_chance_mean can differ numerically from the real-tree arms' -- read it from this arm's own scoring run (recorded under 'baselines_randomdag' in the merged Task 6 JSON when it differs from 'baselines'; p2_verdict falls back to the shared 'baselines' block when a dedicated one is not present, and that fallback is stated explicitly in the code so it cannot pass as a hidden assumption).

declared_confounds: Visibility 0% trains on far fewer retained pairs than visibility 50%, so the two arms take very different numbers of optimizer steps per epoch. vis00 vs vis50 is NOT a controlled contrast on compute; any comparison between them is descriptive, never a causal claim about the visibility knob alone.

The candidate pool is the grandparent's children, so pool size varies from 2 to tens of thousands across held-out nodes. mean_rank is therefore NOT comparable across strata or across arms with different pool-size distributions (vis00/vis50 vs randomdag, whose rewiring changes fan-out); normalized_rank ((rank-1)/(pool-1)) is the comparable quantity.

Held-out leaves are, by construction, the SHALLOWEST leaves in the eligible band: deeper leaves fall outside the declared depth window [11, 28] (Task 1/2) and are never candidates for holdout. Any generalisation claim is scoped to that depth band, not to the full tree.

Held-out nodes are EXEMPT from visibility thinning (Task 2), so at every visibility setting they retain exactly depth-1 ancestry rows -- more of their own ancestry than a random RETAINED node does at visibility 0.5, where retained nodes are thinned. This exemption is deliberate, not an oversight: without it, held-out nodes would appear in zero training rows at visibility 0.0 and would carry untrained embeddings, making the floor gate meaningless at that visibility. It does mean vis00 and vis50 are not comparable on 'how much ancestry did the held-out node see during training' -- that quantity is held out of the thinning by design at both settings.

metrics.primary_reason: The candidate pool is the grandparent's children -- all candidates share the query's grandparent and therefore the SAME target radius (this project established the radius is PLANTED: initialised at the depth's target value and regularised back to it). A depth-homogeneous pool means the planted radius cannot discriminate among candidates AT ALL; ranking on it would be chance. The ranking is angular structure alone, by construction of the pool -- which is exactly the answer to the objection that the headline metric is planted. Poincare distance is still computed and stored as a secondary metric on the identical pools (metrics_poincare), so the choice can be revisited in analysis without re-running anything.

validity_gate: P2 HAS NO TRAINING-LOSS GATE (ruled 2026-09-24, after two prior gate failures on the training-loss proxy -- see 'why'). Three gates, all operating on the metric of interest or on a fact about the run, never on loss: (a) LEARNING GATE -- max_t MRR(t) - MRR(init) > 10 x within-run jitter SD, where MRR(t) is the run's own primary-metric trajectory and MRR(init) is the primary metric at that run's earliest scored checkpoint (P2's scorer records no separate untrained-embedding baseline the way S_angle's init_null does, so the run's own first checkpoint stands in for it). This measures the quantity of interest directly rather than a proxy for it, and a zero or non-finite jitter SD FAILS the gate outright rather than trivially passing it (a degenerate zero-variance fixture must never collapse the 10x threshold to zero and let any rise through -- that exact bug shipped once already in this project's test suite). (b) FLOOR GATE -- an arm-seed whose per-run MRR does not exceed baselines.sibling_chance_mean is UNINFORMATIVE, not a result: a model at chance has said nothing about generalisation, whatever its loss did. (c) COMPLETION CHECK -- the declared final checkpoint (epoch 200) must exist among the scored checkpoints. This is a FACT about the run (a file either exists and was scored, or it does not), not an inference about training dynamics, so unlike a loss-shape gate it cannot misread a converged run as diverged or vice versa. Any of (a)/(b)/(c) failing for ANY seed of ANY arm (including the RandomDAG control) makes the WHOLE verdict UNINFORMATIVE, never a directional read in either direction -- same precedence as the Task 8/9 engine. Training loss per checkpoint is still recorded in full (see metrics.secondary) so a reader can look at it, but it is deliberately absent from every gate; that omission is the fix, not an oversight, and this sentence is the record of the reasoning so a future editor cannot quietly reintroduce a loss gate.

readings.GENERALISES: For a real-tree arm (vis00 or vis50): all 3 seeds' per-run MRR exceed baselines.sibling_chance_mean by >= 2x that arm's pooled within-arm seed SD (a margin condition, checked on the minimum seed so a single weak seed cannot be averaged away), AND all 3 seeds' MRR exceed all 3 of the RandomDAG arm's seeds' MRR (all-above-all, mirroring the Task 8/9 engine's a_above/b_above), AND the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) MRR at the final checkpoint holds in every depth stratum with n >= 500. This is the answer to Burkhard: the model predicts relations it never saw, on a taxonomy it could not have memorised the shape of alone (RandomDAG shares that shape). Overall verdict is GENERALISES only if BOTH vis00 and vis50 reach it independently.
readings.MEMORISES: An arm's per-run MRR sits at or is not meaningfully separated from the floor (fails the >=2x-SD margin above chance), OR the arm is statistically indistinguishable from the RandomDAG control (seed ranges overlap, or |mean difference| is inside an equivalence band of max(0.01, 2x pooled seed SD)). Figure 4-class structure is then in-sample only; the manuscript must say so rather than claim generalisation.
readings.MIXED: The sign of (arm - RandomDAG) flips across depth strata, or the two real-tree arms (vis00, vis50) reach different readings from each other. Reported per stratum and per arm; no single aggregate claim is made.
readings.UNINFORMATIVE: Any of gates (a)/(b)/(c) fails for any seed of any arm, including RandomDAG. A failed gate always wins over every other reading, same as the Task 8/9 engine -- never read a direction out of an invalid run.

p2_amendment_1_20260924.derivation: helpers/p2_randomdag_changes_the_chance_floor.py is a read-only measurement over the mollusca_6447_clean closure (seed 0) that exists independently of any P2 training run: it calls randomdag.randomize_parents directly on the real closure and compares fan-out and sibling_chance before vs after rewiring. No embedding, no checkpoint, no trained model was involved in producing the table below.
p2_amendment_1_20260924.what_it_changes: The CROSS-TREE comparison only -- an arm (vis00 or vis50, scored against the real taxonomy) vs the RandomDAG control (scored against a randomised taxonomy). An arm's OWN validity gates (a/b/c, all on its own tree) and its own floor margin (own MRR vs its own baselines.sibling_chance_mean) are UNCHANGED -- those are within-tree and unaffected by this defect. vis00-vs-vis50 is also UNCHANGED -- both real-tree, same pools, MRR remains comparable there.
the_defect: randomdag.randomize_parents draws each non-root node's new parent uniformly at random from the level above, preserving DEPTH exactly (so the closure pair count -- sum of depths -- is preserved exactly, per its own docstring) but NOT preserving FAN-OUT: a real taxonomy's fan-out is heavy-tailed (a few genera with hundreds of children, most nodes with one or two), so uniform reassignment collapses most randomised grandparents toward 1-2 children.

Measured on mollusca_6447_clean, seed 0: mean fan-out over nodes with >=1 child 4.61 (real tree) vs 1.96 (randomised); max fan-out 187 vs 14; internal nodes 6,946 vs 16,343; leaves 25,071 vs 15,674; band-eligible leaves (depth in [11,28]) 7,405 vs 6,070; mean sibling_chance (1/grandparent fan-out, P2's chance floor) 0.10330 (real) vs 0.55816 (randomised); median sibling_chance 0.0417 vs 0.5000.

Mean chance-floor ratio randomised/real = 5.403. RandomDAG's held-out task is therefore, on average, ~5.4x EASIER at chance than the real-tree task it exists to control for -- a materially DIFFERENT-DIFFICULTY task, not merely a scrambled one.

Consequence for the frozen reading: the readings above compare an arm's raw MRR head-to-head against RandomDAG's raw MRR (all-above-all on MRR; an equivalence band computed on MRR). Because RandomDAG's own chance floor is ~5.4x higher, RandomDAG can out-score (or tie) a real, genuinely-generalising arm on raw MRR almost regardless of what the model learned -- which the frozen rule reads as MEMORISES or MIXED. A false MEMORISES verdict is the single worst outcome this control exists to avoid, since it would be read as refuting Figure 4-class generalisation when the geometry never had the chance to demonstrate it on equal footing.
p2_amendment_1_20260924.declared_confound_5: RandomDAG rewiring preserves each node's DEPTH exactly but not its FAN-OUT: mean chance-floor ratio randomised/real = 5.403 on mollusca_6447_clean seed 0 (see the_defect above, and helpers/p2_randomdag_changes_the_chance_floor.py). RandomDAG is therefore a DIFFERENT-DIFFICULTY task, not merely a scrambled one -- which is why every cross-tree read (an arm vs RandomDAG) is chance-normalised (normalized_rank), never raw MRR, under this amendment.

the_correction.rule_1: Any CROSS-TREE comparison (an arm vs RandomDAG) uses normalized_rank = (rank-1)/(pool-1), never MRR. Under a random ranking, rank is uniform on 1..pool, so E[normalized_rank] = ((pool-1)/2)/(pool-1) = 0.5 for EVERY pool size -- exactly the pool-size (and so fan-out) invariance the real-vs-RandomDAG comparison needs. Lower normalized_rank is better. WITHIN-tree comparisons (vis00 vs vis50; an arm vs its OWN sibling_chance_mean) still use MRR as primary: same tree, same pools, comparable, and untouched by this defect.
the_correction.rule_2: Each arm is read against its OWN chance floor -- already true in the frozen implementation (p2_verdict reads baselines_randomdag.sibling_chance_mean for the control and baselines.sibling_chance_mean for vis00/vis50, via p2_group_stats called once per arm with that arm's own floor). This amendment does not change that; it is restated here because it is the within-tree half of the same principle whose cross-tree half (rule_1) this amendment fixes -- never compare an arm's MRR to the OTHER tree's floor.
the_correction.rule_3: GENERALISES (amended): the arm's own MRR still clears its own sibling_chance_mean by the original margin (>= 2x pooled within-arm seed SD, own-tree, unchanged -- checked on the weakest/minimum seed) AND the arm's normalized_rank sits below every RandomDAG seed's normalized_rank (all-below-all, the direct mirror of the frozen all-above-all-on-MRR condition -- no run of the arm may be at or above any run of the control) AND the arm's normalized_rank is below the pool-size-invariant chance level of 0.5 on its weakest (highest) seed AND the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) normalized_rank is negative in every depth stratum with n>=500. MEMORISES (amended): the arm fails its own MRR margin, OR its normalized_rank is statistically indistinguishable from RandomDAG's normalized_rank (seed ranges overlap, or |mean difference| < max(0.01, 2x pooled seed SD), all computed on normalized_rank). MIXED (amended): the sign of (arm - RandomDAG) normalized_rank flips across depth strata, or vis00 and vis50 reach different readings from each other (unchanged from the frozen rule).

p2_amendment_3_20260924.why: A final whole-branch review found that the pre-registration, as it stood after amendment_2, would currently return a POSITIVE (GENERALISES) verdict for a model that learned nothing: a training-free degree prior (rank candidates by child count, descending) already clears the frozen GENERALISES bar on the real metazoa split. Four further defects were found while fixing it: a chance-level confusion in gate (b), a free win at pool size 1 that flatters exactly the wrong arm, a manifest path absent inside the LRZ container, and independent breaks that made the scorer's real output shape unparseable by the verdict engine. Each is recorded below with what was wrong, the fix, and where the fix lives in code.

c1_degree_prior_baseline.the_defect: Held-out leaves (Task 1/2) are sampled UNIFORMLY from band-eligible leaves, so a candidate parent with more children is more likely to be the TRUE parent of a randomly sampled leaf -- a fact about the SAMPLING, needing no embedding and no training at all. Measured on the real metazoa split (seed 0, POST the C3 fix below -- pool-size-1 queries excluded from this baseline's own score exactly as from every other): ranking the grandparent's children by descending child count alone scores MRR 0.5600, hits@1 0.4039, normalized_rank 0.1538 (helpers/p2_degree_prior_and_chance_verify.py) -- comfortably above the analytic chance MRR (0.2711) and above the RandomDAG control's own score at the same task. The frozen readings.GENERALISES text only required beating chance and beating RandomDAG; this training-free ranker clears both, so a model that learned nothing about the taxonomy -- only that high-fanout nodes make likelier parents, itself just a restatement of the sampling procedure -- would read GENERALISES.
c1_degree_prior_baseline.the_fix: src/taxembed/eval/baselines.py::degree_prior_rank / degree_prior_metrics compute this baseline (candidates ranked by descending fan-out, ties broken by the SAME seeded jitter taxembed.eval.linkpred.rank_of_true_parent uses, so index order cannot leak into either ranker). scripts/score_p2_linkpred.py computes it once per manifest/heldout pair (never per checkpoint, mirroring sibling_chance_mean/vendrov_recall/majority_parent_rate) and writes it under baselines.degree_prior = {mrr, hits_at_1, hits_at_10, normalized_rank, n, n_scored, n_trivial}. src/taxembed/eval/preregistration.py::_p2_arm_reading adds a new REQUIRED condition to GENERALISES in BOTH the amendment_1=False (raw MRR) and amendment_1=True (normalized_rank) branches: the arm's own MRR (resp. normalized_rank) must beat its OWN tree's degree_prior MRR (resp. normalized_rank). An arm that does not is read MEMORISES, never GENERALISES, regardless of how it compares to chance or to RandomDAG.

c2_chance_mrr_mean.the_defect: The pre-fix src/taxembed/eval/preregistration.py gated on per_run_value > sibling_chance_mean, where sibling_chance_mean = mean(1/k) is the chance rate for HITS@1 -- the probability a uniformly random SINGLE guess is correct. per_run_value is an MRR, and a uniformly random RANKER's own expected MRR is mean(H_k/k) (H_k = the k-th harmonic number), which is ALWAYS larger than mean(1/k) for k>1 (H_k>1). Measured on the real metazoa split: chance_mrr_mean 0.27107 vs sibling_chance_mean (hits@1 chance) 0.13126 -- a 2.065x gap. metrics_poincare_is_not_independent_corr.the_claim: On a depth-homogeneous candidate pool where every candidate shares one hyperbolic radius (true by construction: P2's pool is the grandparent's children, all at the query's parent's depth, and this project's own established finding -- this file's metrics.primary_reason -- is that radius is PLANTED, initialised at the depth's target value and regularised back to it), the exact (law-of-cosines) Poincare distance is a STRICTLY MONOTONIC function of cosine distance for ANY fixed query radius: cosh(d) = cosh(r_u)cosh(R) - sinh(r_u)sinh(R)cos(theta), and with r_u and R both fixed across the candidate set, cosh(d) is a decreasing affine function of cos(theta) alone (sinh(r_u)sinh(R) > 0 for any non-root node). Ranking candidates 'nearest first' by either metric therefore produces the IDENTICAL order -- and since metrics_cosine/metrics_poincare are both pure functions of the rank order (taxembed.eval.linkpred.linkpred_metrics), they are then NUMERICALLY IDENTICAL, not merely correlated. metrics_poincare is therefore NOT independent corroboration of a cosine-primary reading -- it is the SAME ranking read through a monotone reparametrisation, and must never be reported as a second, agreeing measurement.
metrics_poincare_is_not_independent_corr.how_this_was_verified: NOT on a real trained checkpoint -- none exists; the pre-registration is frozen before any P2 array has run, and this session made no training run (hard boundary: no cluster submission). The claim was instead verified structurally, against the PRODUCTION taxembed.eval.linkpred._poincare_distance/_cosine_distance functions: 500 random configurations with all candidates sharing one radius (query radius independently randomised) gave IDENTICAL cosine and exact-Poincare rankings in every trial (0/500 mismatches); a control of 500 configurations with candidate radii independently randomised gave 467/500 mismatches, confirming the equal-radius condition is load-bearing, not vacuously always true. On an ACTUAL trained checkpoint, near-identity depends on how tightly the radial regulariser holds same-depth candidates to a common radius -- expected to be very tight per this project's own established finding, but this session did not and could not measure that tightness on a live run, and this correction should be read with that scope. Compute metrics_poincare or drop it -- this note does not decide that -- but report it as the SAME ranking under a monotone reparametrisation, never as agreement between two independent readings.
metrics_poincare_is_not_independent_corr.verified_by: a one-off, not-checked-in script mirroring tests/eval/test_linkpred.py's existing exact-vs-ball-coordinate Poincare distance tests: 500/500 equal-radius trials, 0 ranking mismatches; 500/500 unequal-radius control trials, 467 mismatches.

p2_amendment_4_20260924.why: p2_amendment_1_20260924 established that randomize_parents draws each node's new parent UNIFORMLY AT RANDOM (i.i.d., with replacement) from the level above, which does not preserve fan-out: a real taxonomy's fan-out is heavy-tailed (a few genera with hundreds of children, most nodes with one or two), so i.i.d. resampling regresses every parent's child count toward the mean. Measured on mollusca_6447_clean seed 0: mean fan-out 4.61 -> 1.96, max fan-out 187 -> 14, raising the mean chance floor (sibling_chance) 5.403x. The training-free degree prior (baselines.degree_prior_rank, p2_amendment_3_20260924's C1) is directly downstream of the same defect: normalized_rank 0.1538 on the real tree but 0.2487 on the randomised one -- i.e. the control that is supposed to be the FLOOR a genuine model must clear is itself WORSE at the training-free prior than the real tree, which is exactly the gap that lets a learned-nothing model clear `above_control_all_seeds`/`below_control_all_seeds`. The fix is a control that preserves fan-out by construction rather than by chance.
p2_amendment_4_20260924.the_replacement: A configuration-model shuffle: at each depth level d, permute the ACTUAL multiset of parent labels that depth-d nodes already carry (one label per depth-d node -- a parent with k children at depth d contributes k copies of its own index to that multiset) via a uniform random permutation, and reassign the permuted labels back to the SAME depth-d nodes. Every parent that had k children at depth d still has EXACTLY k children at depth d afterward -- a bijection on a fixed multiset, never an i.i.d. resample -- so the global fan-out multiset (and therefore each node's OWN fan-out, individually, not merely in aggregate) is preserved EXACTLY, verified elementwise on mollusca_6447_clean (0 of 32,017 nodes differ). depth is preserved exactly (only which SAME-depth node a parent label attaches to changes, never which depth level), so the closure pair count (sum of depth) is preserved exactly, and no node can become its own ancestor. src/taxembed/eval/randomdag.py::degree_matched_shuffle; scripts/build_p2_degmatch_split.py builds the two matched splits (--visibility 0.0, --visibility 0.5) from it, mirroring scripts/build_p2_randomdag_split.py's shape exactly.

measured_on_mollusca_6447_clean_seed0.fanout_per_node_identical_elementwise: verified separately (0 of 32,017 nodes differ) -- a STRICTLY STRONGER property than the sorted-multiset check, since a construction could satisfy the multiset check without preserving any single node's own fan-out; degree_matched_shuffle satisfies both because it is a per-node bijection, not merely a distribution match.

p2_amendment_4_20260924.the_result_is_an_improvement_not_full_pa: The task this amendment implements expected the degree-matched shuffle to make the chance floor and the degree prior MATCH between the two trees. Measured, they do NOT match exactly: the residual sibling_chance_mean ratio is 1.84x (down from RandomDAG's 5.403x, a 2.9x reduction in the gap, but not 1.0x). REASON, derived from the same measurement, not assumed: degree_matched_shuffle preserves each node's OWN fan-out (a ONE-HOP quantity) exactly, but P2's chance floor and degree prior are TWO-HOP quantities (a held-out leaf's GRANDPARENT's fan-out). Preserving fan-out at every depth level independently does not preserve the JOINT distribution between a leaf's position and its grandparent's fan-out: composing two independent per-level permutations effectively resamples a leaf's grandparent via a fan-out-size-biased draw (a node with more children is proportionally more likely to end up as some leaf's NEW parent, and by the same mechanism one level up, some leaf's NEW grandparent), which is not how grandparent-fan-out was distributed among leaves in the real taxonomy. A degree-matched shuffle is therefore a SUBSTANTIAL improvement over RandomDAG (the confound this amendment exists to close is smaller by a factor of ~2.9), not a complete equalisation of the cross-tree comparison's difficulty. This is a measured finding, not the outcome the amendment's design assumed, and is recorded here rather than silently reported as full parity -- 'should' is the word that precedes every silent defect in this build (project convention), so it was measured instead of assumed.
p2_amendment_4_20260924.consequence_amendment_1_stays_load_beari: p2_amendment_1_20260924's normalized_rank rule (rule_1: any CROSS-TREE comparison uses normalized_rank, never raw MRR, because normalized_rank's chance level is exactly 0.5 for EVERY pool size) was motivated by the 5.4x chance-floor gap RandomDAG produced. Because amendment_4's degree-matched control REDUCES that gap to ~1.84x but does not CLOSE it, amendment_1's rule remains LOAD-BEARING for the cross-tree (arm vs control) comparison, not merely belt-and-braces as originally anticipated: raw MRR is still not directly comparable between the real tree and the degree-matched control's pools. the_defect.summary: GENERALISES was STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE under the reading production computes (amendment_1 + amendment_2 + amendment_4). amendment_1 moved the cross-tree comparison to normalized_rank, which removes the POOL-SIZE (fan-out) confound. the_amendment.rule_1_own_prior_ratio: Every CROSS-TREE quantity is read as a RATIO to the arm's OWN tree's training-free degree prior: (arm_nr / arm_own_prior_nr) vs (control_nr / control_own_prior_nr). 1.0 is exactly 'no better than what this tree hands out for free' on either side, so the comparison asks which model improved MORE on its own baseline, and is invariant to the difficulty gap by construction. The scorer already emits a degree_prior block per --baselines-key, so the control's own prior was already on disk; the reading simply never used it.
the_amendment.rule_2_relative_equivalence_band: The normalized_rank equivalence band becomes max(P2_EQUIV_REL_FRACTION * |control_mean|, P2_FLOOR_SD_MULTIPLE * pooled_sd) with P2_EQUIV_REL_FRACTION = 0.05, replacing max(P2_EQUIV_FLOOR, ...). P2_EQUIV_FLOOR = 0.01 was calibrated on MRR (~0.8 in production, so ~1.2%); applied unchanged to normalized_rank (~0.04) it was ~25% of the compared quantity. Measured consequence, review scenario S3: two arms differing by 0.2% read equivalent_to_control=True on |mean_diff| = 0.00008, i.e. an automatic MEMORISES.
the_amendment.rule_3_generalises_requires_distinguisha: GENERALISES now additionally requires `not equivalent_to_control`. FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING THIS AMENDMENT, pre-run, by helpers/p2_amendment6_reachability.py scenario R2: `below_control_all_seeds` is a strict max<min, so a mathematical TIE is settled by the last bit of floating point. On the review's EXPECTED case -- arm and control improving on their own priors by the SAME factor -- the engine returned GENERALISES while reporting |mean_diff| = 0.000000 and equivalent_to_control = True in the same dict. The MEMORISES branch does test that boolean, but it is an elif and never ran. A verdict that contradicts its own reported booleans is not a reading.
the_amendment.rule_4_mixed_prose_names_the_binding_cla: The MIXED verdict string is now derived from the clause that actually bound. FOUND pre-run by the same probe, scenario R3: the MIXED branch is reachable for three different reasons (a depth-stratum sign flip, the arm failing to beat its control on every seed, or normalized_rank not clearing 0.5) but its prose asserted the first unconditionally. On an arm uniformly WORSE than its control there is no flip anywhere and the published sentence was simply untrue. A verdict string is quoted into the manuscript.

stated_limitations.strata_use_the_aggregate_prior: The per-depth-stratum sign test applies the same own-prior scaling, but the scorer emits degree_prior only as an AGGREGATE (scripts/score_p2_linkpred.py writes one block per --baselines-key, with no by_depth breakdown), so each side is divided by its tree's aggregate prior rather than a per-stratum one. This is a uniform positive rescaling of each side: it cannot reorder strata within an arm, and what it does is relax the cross-tree sign test by the measured difficulty ratio. A per-stratum prior would be sharper and is NOT claimed.

p2_amendment_6_20260926.corrects_amendment_4: p2_amendment_4_20260924's `the_replacement` states the degree-matched shuffle preserves 'the chance floor and the degree prior ... by construction'. MEASURED, that is false for the degree prior: per-node fan-out IS preserved elementwise (0 of 498,246 differ, confirmed at metazoa scale), but the degree PRIOR's normalized_rank is 0.1538 on the real tree vs 0.0404 on the control. Against the RETIRED RandomDAG control the same mismatch was 0.1538 vs 0.2487. In |log-ratio| the mismatch is 1.34 under the live control vs 0.48 under RandomDAG: amendment_4 made the degree-prior gap 2.8x LARGER in magnitude while FLIPPING ITS SIGN. The flip is what closes C1 (a fan-out-only model can no longer clear the control) and is a genuine improvement; the growth is what made GENERALISES unreachable. amendment_4's `the_result_is_an_improvement_not_full_parity` block concedes the chance-floor residual (1.84x on mollusca; 1.39-1.44x measured at metazoa) but records nothing about the degree-prior gap, and that omission is what hid this finding until the final review.
p2_amendment_6_20260926.corrects_amendment_3: p2_amendment_3_20260924's c3 block asserts that chance_mrr_mean 'inherits the [k=1] exclusion for free'. It does not: chance_mrr_mean averages H_k/k over ALL k INCLUDING k=1, while every metric it anchors excludes k=1. Measured on the production splits: the as-coded value is +10.5% (real) and +23.1% (degmatch) above the k>=2 value, and sibling_chance_mean +30.6%. The k=1-inclusive behaviour is PINNED BY A TEST and is conservative for our own margin, but it inflates the CONTROL's gate-(b) floor by ~23%, which is a live UNINFORMATIVE risk rather than a safe direction. Corrected here as a statement of record; the behaviour is left as coded and tested.

generalises_no_longer_implies_out_rankin.the_disclosure: THE MOST IMPORTANT ENTRY IN THIS AMENDMENT. Under amendment_6 the cross-tree comparison is a RATIO to each tree's own training-free degree prior, so GENERALISES means 'the arm improved MORE on its own tree's prior than the control did on its own' -- it does NOT mean 'the arm ranked the true parent better than the control did'. Measured through the real engine: an arm whose control out-ranks it 2.25x on raw normalized_rank reads GENERALISES, and so does an arm scoring EXACTLY what its control scores. The GENERALISES window extends to a raw ratio of about 3.6x, which is the measured difficulty gap, so this is a wide region and not a corner case.
generalises_no_longer_implies_out_rankin.why_this_is_the_intended_reading_and_sti: It IS the question the design intends: the control's task is ~3.8x easier for a training-free ranker, so equal raw scores mean the arm did more. That is precisely what amendment_6 exists to express. But the verdict's own prose ('the model predicts relations it never saw') reads to any ordinary reader as a claim that the arm beat its control outright, and a manuscript sentence built on it would be wrong in a way nobody could detect from the published verdict.
generalises_no_longer_implies_out_rankin.what_changed: The reading now always carries `raw_mean_diff_vs_control`, `arm_beats_control_raw`, `arm_values_raw_normalized_rank` and `control_values_raw_normalized_rank`, and scripts/apply_preregistration.py prints them beside the ratio values, with an explicit warning line when GENERALISES is returned while arm_beats_control_raw is False. NOTHING IS GATED ON THEM: whether the raw comparison should also have to pass is a design decision for the USER, and taking it silently here would be the same class of error as the one being corrected.

p2_amendment_7_20260926.per_seed_own_prior_denominators: CORRECTION to amendment_6 as implemented. It divided all three seeds by SEED 0's own-prior, because p2_group_stats' group-level `degree_prior` comes from seeds[0]. That was defensible before amendment_6 -- the function's docstring argues the group-level block is cosmetic because each seed's GATE already uses its own dict -- and amendment_6 falsified it by making that value the DENOMINATOR of the published statistic. Measured on the project's own per-seed priors the choice alone flips the verdict (MEMORISES with the seed-0 denominator, GENERALISES with per-seed ones): the control's cross-seed prior spread is ~5.4%, the same order as the 5% decision band it feeds. Each seed now divides by its own seed's prior; the seed-0 scalar is retained for display only.

per_stratum_own_prior_denominators.the_correction: amendment_6's stated_limitations.strata_use_the_aggregate_prior defended dividing every depth stratum by the AGGREGATE prior on the grounds that it 'cannot reorder strata within an arm'. True, and beside the point: sign_consistent is a CROSS-ARM test, so what matters is whether the aggregate difficulty ratio equals the per-stratum one. It does not.

per_stratum_own_prior_denominators.the_fix: scripts/score_p2_linkpred.py now emits degree_prior.by_depth, stratified with the same bins and the same reducer a checkpoint's ranks get, and _p2_depth_means divides each stratum by that stratum's own prior. The reading records depth_strata.stratum_prior_basis, including used_per_stratum_priors, so a fallback to the aggregate on an older scorer output can never be silent.

the_ruling.verdict: REJECTED, 2026-09-28, before any P2 number was read. No gate is added. The verdict stays the amendment_6 ratio reading: the arm's improvement over its OWN tree's training-free degree prior, compared with the degree-matched control's improvement over ITS own prior. The raw head-to-head continues to be REPORTED beside it, exactly as the engine already does.
the_ruling.user_words_verbatim: If we are controlling how fast a runner runs, then making control run on a better tarmac is not fair.
the_ruling.the_reasoning: The degree-matched control's task is ~3.8x EASIER for a training-free ranker (degree-prior normalized_rank 0.1538 real vs 0.0404 degmatch, measured on these very production splits and independently re-derived 2026-09-26). A raw-score gate would therefore require the arm to beat a number its control gets for free by virtue of an easier task -- penalising the arm for the CONTROL'S tarmac, not for anything the model did or failed to do. That is the identical defect amendment_6 was written to remove; re-introducing it as an additional gate would reinstate it under a different name and, per helpers/p2_amendment6_reachability.py scenario R5, would again make GENERALISES structurally unreachable even for a checkpoint that saw every held-out edge.

A sentence claiming the arm simply beat its control would be wrong, and the raw fields printed beside the verdict are what makes that detectable.
